h1: The 7 Best Cordless Pruning Saws Under $100, Chain and Reciprocating, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Cordless Pruning Saw Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cordless pruning saws under $100, chain and reciprocating types, compared on bar size, batteries and kit contents.
summary: The 21V 2.0Ah 6-inch pruning saw is the best cordless pruning saw under $100 for most people, a light one-hand saw that costs under $25. The Greenworks 24V 6in is the brand-backed kit, the Greenworks 4 inch is the lightest, and the RYOBI one-handed reciprocating saw is the pick for tight shrubs if you own a ONE+ battery.
intro: Under $100 there are two different tools sold as cordless pruning saws, and mixing them up is expensive. A chain-type pruner is a small chainsaw built for branches. A reciprocating saw is a push-pull blade tool that cuts quietly and safely, but only works well with the right pruning blade. The best buyers decide which style they want before they look at price.

This ranking sorts seven options by style, kit contents and bar length. We reviewed the listings supplied, and a higher-priced Greenworks pruner was left out because it sits above the budget. Reciprocating saws are included because they do prune well with the right blade, but we flag where a listing is a general-purpose tool instead of a purpose-built pruner.

products.name: 6-Inch Mini Chainsaw Cordless, 21V 2.0Ah Battery Powered Electric Pruning Saw, One-Hand Chain Saw for Tree Trimming
products.verdict: A light 6 inch, 21V, 2.0Ah pruning saw for beginners and seniors at the lowest cost.
products.description:
This pruning saw has a 6 inch bar and a 21V, 2.0Ah battery, marketed as lightweight and easy to control for beginners, seniors and general yard work. Cost is less than $25.

It claims first place on value: it is a complete battery-powered pruner for a fraction of the cost of a branded kit. The one-hand design and low weight suit people who dislike heavy tools. The 2.0Ah battery is a respectable size for a saw at this price, but there is only one, and you cannot trade a flat pack for a fresh one mid-job.

Buy it for light trimming and easy handling. Skip it if you want a branded warranty.
products.idealFor: Beginners and seniors with light trimming.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 6in Mini Chainsaw, 2.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A 6 inch Greenworks pruner that comes with a 2.0 Ah battery and a charger.
products.description:
The Greenworks has a 6 inch bar and the 24V battery platform, with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger in the box. Cost runs $50 to $100.

Placement in second comes from the fact that it is the same size as the leader but backed by a mainstream outdoor brand. That means a clearer warranty path, available spare chains and a battery that powers other Greenworks 24V tools. You pay noticeably more than the $25 option for those assurances.

Buy it if brand support matters. Skip it if the cheapest complete kit is your goal.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 4 in Mini Chainsaw, 2.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: The smallest Greenworks saw, with a 4 inch bar and a 2.0 Ah battery and charger.
products.description:
The 4 inch Greenworks is a very compact saw that comes with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger. Cost runs $50 to $100.

Placement in third comes from the fact that the 4 inch bar limits you to thin branches, but it is the easiest to control. For rose pruning, hedging and cutting thin stems, a smaller, lighter saw reduces fatigue. Compared with the 6 inch version, you give up cutting capacity for handling.

Choose it for thin stems and tight spots. Skip it if you cut anything thicker than a thumb.

products.name: RYOBI 18V ONE+ One-Handed Pruning Reciprocating Saw Tool Only
products.verdict: A one-handed RYOBI reciprocating pruning saw for ONE+ owners, sold without a battery.
products.description:
This RYOBI ONE+ saw is a one-handed reciprocating pruning tool sold tool only. It costs $50 to $100 and needs an 18V ONE+ battery.

It ranks fourth because it is a purpose-built pruning reciprocating saw rather than a general demolition tool, which makes it lighter and easier to hold. There is no chain, so no oiling and less kickback concern. It is slower on thick wood and needs a battery you may not own.

Buy it if you have RYOBI batteries and like a blade saw. Skip it if you have none.
pros: No chain to oil or tension

products.name: SEESII Reciprocating Saw Cordless with 2 x 4.0Ah Batteries and 6 Saw Blades
products.verdict: A reciprocating saw with two 4.0Ah batteries and six blades, a general tool that prunes well with the right blade.
products.description:
The SEESII is a cordless reciprocating saw sold with two 4.0Ah batteries and six saw blades. Cost runs $50 to $100.

Placement in fifth comes from the fact that it is a general-purpose tool, not a dedicated pruner. It is bigger and heavier than the small chain saws and needs two hands, but the batteries and blades make it a good all-round kit. With a coarse pruning blade it cuts branches well, and with other blades it handles wood, plastic and light demolition.

Buy it if you want a pruner that doubles as a workshop tool. Skip it if you want a light one-hand saw.
products.idealFor: DIYers who also cut wood and pipe.
products.skipIf: You want a light, one-hand pruner.

products.name: ONEAND 18V 6 in. Cordless Battery Compact Pruning MINI Chainsaw Tool ONLY
products.verdict: A 6 inch, 18V chain pruner sold tool only, with a thin listing.
products.description:
The ONEAND is an 18V, 6 inch compact pruning mini chainsaw sold tool only. Cost runs $50 to $100.

Placement in sixth comes from the fact that the listing does not say which battery brands fit, or give motor details. That makes it a gamble even for someone with 18V batteries at home. If the battery fits, it is a cheap way to add a chain pruner.

Buy it only after you verify battery fit. Skip it if you want a guarantee.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX* Cordless Reciprocating Saw Kit (BDCR20C)
products.verdict: A well-known 20V MAX reciprocating saw kit, general purpose rather than a dedicated pruner.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER BDCR20C is a 20V MAX cordless reciprocating saw kit. It costs $50 to $100.

It ranks last as a pruning tool because it is a general DIY saw, not designed for one-hand pruning. The brand is trusted and parts are easy to find, and with a pruning blade it will cut branches, but weight and size make it tiring overhead.

Buy it if you need a general cordless saw that can also prune. Skip it if pruning is the main job.

whatMatters.detail: Chain pruners cut fast in green wood but need oil. Reciprocating saws are quiet and need only a blade. Choose the style for the work and your comfort with chains.
Bare-tool listings leave out the battery and charger. These can cost as much as the tool. Look for tool only in the title.
Pruning often means reaching and holding a branch with the other hand. A saw under about two pounds helps. Check weight and the one-hand wording.
A reciprocating saw needs a pruning blade with coarse teeth, while a chain pruner needs a sharp chain. Check what is supplied.
A 2.0Ah battery lasts for a few trees. Two 4.0Ah batteries give long sessions. Match battery capacity to the size of your garden.

faq.q: Can a reciprocating saw prune trees?
faq.a: Yes, with a coarse pruning blade. It is slower than a chain pruner but quieter and simpler. Use the correct blade for green wood.
Buying a tool-only saw without a battery. Check the title for the words tool only before ordering.

faq.q: Is Greenworks worth it over the 21V budget saw?
faq.a: If you value a warranty and platform, yes. For occasional trimming, the 21V saw gives more value.

finalTake: The 21V 2.0Ah 6 inch pruning saw is the best cordless pruning saw under $100, a light complete kit under $25. The Greenworks 24V 6in is the branded choice, the Greenworks 4 in suits thin stems, and the RYOBI one-handed reciprocating saw is the pick for ONE+ owners. Check for tool only wording before you pay.
